subject: US-260: Real-Time WebSocket Integration for Admin Analytics
description:
# US-260: Real-Time WebSocket Integration for Admin Analytics

## Objective
Implement WebSocket integration for live metrics streaming in SPEC-030 Admin Analytics Console, replacing polling-based updates with true real-time data.

## Technical Tasks

### 1. Backend WebSocket Endpoint
- Create WebSocket endpoint `/admin-analytics/ws`
- Implement connection management (connect, disconnect, reconnection handling)
- Stream metrics updates every 5 seconds
- Handle concurrent admin user connections
- Graceful error handling and connection cleanup

### 2. Frontend WebSocket Client
- Implement WebSocket connection in admin-analytics.html and Analytics.tsx
- Automatic reconnection logic with exponential backoff
- Handle connection state (connected, disconnected, reconnecting)
- Update dashboard metrics in real-time without page refresh
- Display connection status indicator

### 3. Metrics Streaming
Stream the following metrics in real-time:
- Active sessions count
- API requests per minute
- New signups today
- Revenue today
- System load, memory usage
- Database connections
- Cache hit rate
- Error rate (5-minute window)
- P95 response time

### 4. Integration with SPEC-070
- Reuse SPEC-070 WebSocket infrastructure where possible
- Standardize message format across both dashboards
- Share WebSocket connection pooling if applicable
- Consistent error handling patterns

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] WebSocket endpoint `/admin-analytics/ws` functional
- [ ] Real-time metrics streaming every 5 seconds
- [ ] Automatic reconnection on connection loss
- [ ] Support 10+ concurrent admin connections
- [ ] Frontend updates metrics without page refresh
- [ ] Connection status visible in UI
- [ ] Performance: <50ms latency for metric updates
- [ ] Graceful degradation if WebSocket unavailable (fallback to polling)
- [ ] WebSocket connection properly cleaned up on disconnect

## Technical Details

### WebSocket Message Format
```json
{
  "type": "metrics_update",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "data": {
    "active_sessions": 234,
    "api_requests_per_minute": 1247,
    "new_signups_today": 23,
    "revenue_today": 1456.78,
    "system_load": 0.67,
    "memory_usage": 0.73,
    "database_connections": 45,
    "cache_hit_rate": 0.94,
    "error_rate_5m": 0.0012,
    "response_time_p95": 167
  }
}
```

### Frontend Integration
```javascript
// Connect to WebSocket
const ws = new WebSocket('ws://localhost:13370/admin-analytics/ws');

ws.onmessage = (event) => {
  const update = JSON.parse(event.data);
  if (update.type === 'metrics_update') {
    updateDashboard(update.data);
  }
};

// Auto-reconnect on close
ws.onclose = () => {
  setTimeout(() => connectWebSocket(), 5000);
};
```

## Dependencies
- SPEC-070: Real-Time Monitoring Dashboard (reuse WebSocket patterns)
- FastAPI WebSocket support
- Frontend WebSocket API support

## Estimated Effort
16-20 hours (2-2.5 days)

## Related
- File: `server/admin_analytics_api.py` (lines 614-637)
- SPEC: SPEC-030 Technical Implementation (WebSocket integration)
- Related: SPEC-070 WebSocket infrastructure

# US-261: Production Data Migration - Remove Mock Data Dependencies

## Objective
Replace all mock data fallbacks in SPEC-030 Admin Analytics API with real database queries and proper activity tracking to enable production-ready analytics.

## Technical Tasks

### 1. Database Schema Review
- Review existing tables: `users`, `teams`, `team_memberships`
- Identify missing tables for activity tracking:
  - User activity/session logs
  - Feature usage tracking
  - API call metrics
  - Login patterns
- Plan schema extensions if needed (Alembic migrations)

### 2. Real Query Implementation
Replace mock data functions with real queries:

#### Platform Overview (`/platform-overview`)
- ✅ `total_users`: Real `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users`
- ✅ `total_teams`: Real `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM teams WHERE is_standalone = true`
- ❌ `active_users_30d`: Currently mocked - implement real query
- ❌ `active_teams_30d`: Currently mocked - implement real query
- ❌ `new_signups_30d`: Currently mocked - implement real query with date filtering
- ❌ `new_teams_30d`: Currently mocked - implement real query
- ⚠️ `total_revenue_30d`: Needs integration with billing/subscription tables
- ✅ `avg_team_size`: Real query exists, verify accuracy

#### Churn Analysis (`/churn-analysis`)
- Implement real churn risk calculation from:
  - Team activity patterns
  - Subscription status
  - Payment failures (if available)
  - Usage decline detection
- Calculate retention by cohort from actual signup dates
- Track churn reasons from cancellation data

#### Revenue Cohorts (`/revenue-cohorts`)
- Query revenue data from billing/subscription tables
- Calculate actual LTV from historical payments
- Track expansion/contraction revenue from subscription changes
- Calculate NRR from actual revenue data

#### User Engagement (`/user-engagement`)
- Implement daily active users from activity logs
- Calculate feature adoption from usage tracking
- Track session duration from session logs
- Calculate engagement scores from actual activity

### 3. Activity Tracking Implementation
If activity tables don't exist:
- Create `user_activities` table (user_id, activity_type, timestamp, metadata)
- Create `user_sessions` table (user_id, session_id, start_time, end_time, actions_count)
- Create `feature_usage` table (user_id, feature_name, usage_count, last_used)
- Implement activity tracking middleware/helpers
- Populate activity data from existing logs if available

### 4. Error Handling
- Remove mock data fallbacks (keep for development/testing only)
- Implement proper error handling:
  - Database connection failures
  - Query timeouts
  - Data not available (return empty/minimal data, not mock)
- Add logging for data quality issues
- Return appropriate HTTP status codes

### 5. Performance Optimization
- Optimize database queries (indexes, query plans)
- Implement query result caching (Redis - separate story)
- Add query performance monitoring
- Set query timeouts
- Consider materialized views for complex aggregations

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All `/platform-overview` metrics use real database queries
- [ ] Churn analysis calculates from real team/user data
- [ ] Revenue cohorts query from actual billing data
- [ ] User engagement metrics use activity tracking
- [ ] No mock data fallbacks in production code path
- [ ] Error handling for all database operations
- [ ] Query performance: <500ms for all endpoints
- [ ] Activity tracking tables created if needed
- [ ] Database migrations tested and applied
- [ ] Code coverage: 80%+ for new queries

## Technical Details

### Active Users Query Example
```python
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from sqlalchemy import func

# Real active users query (last 30 days)
thirty_days_ago = datetime.utcnow() - timedelta(days=30)
active_users = db.query(User).join(
    UserActivity
).filter(
    UserActivity.timestamp >= thirty_days_ago
).distinct().count()
```

### Churn Risk Calculation
```python
def calculate_churn_risk(team: Team, db: Session) -> float:
    """Calculate churn risk score (0-1) based on multiple factors"""
    risk_factors = {
        'low_activity': check_low_activity(team, db),
        'payment_failures': check_payment_failures(team, db),
        'member_departures': check_member_departures(team, db),
        'support_tickets': check_support_tickets(team, db)
    }
    # Weighted scoring algorithm
    risk_score = (
        risk_factors['low_activity'] * 0.3 +
        risk_factors['payment_failures'] * 0.3 +
        risk_factors['member_departures'] * 0.2 +
        risk_factors['support_tickets'] * 0.2
    )
    return min(1.0, risk_score)
```

## Dependencies
- Database schema (users, teams, team_memberships tables)
- Billing/subscription tables (SPEC-026/027)
- Activity tracking infrastructure (may need to create)
- Alembic for migrations

## Estimated Effort
24-30 hours (3-4 days)

## Related
- File: `server/admin_analytics_api.py` (lines 158-637)
- SPEC: SPEC-030 Production Data Requirements
- Related: SPEC-026 (billing data), SPEC-027 (subscription data)

description:
# US-262: Security Monitoring Dashboard for Admin Analytics

## Objective
Implement security monitoring capabilities in SPEC-030 Admin Analytics Console to track authentication failures, suspicious activity patterns, and security-related metrics.

## Technical Tasks

### 1. Authentication Failure Tracking
- Query authentication service logs for failed login attempts
- Track failed login patterns:
  - Failed logins per user (potential account compromise)
  - Failed logins per IP address (potential brute force)
  - Failed logins per time period (identify attack windows)
  - Common failure reasons (wrong password, expired token, invalid credentials)
- Implement rate-based alerts for suspicious patterns

### 2. Suspicious Activity Detection
Track and flag suspicious activities:
- Multiple failed login attempts from same IP
- Login attempts from unusual locations/IPs
- Rapid successive login failures
- Account access from multiple locations simultaneously
- Unusual API usage patterns (potential abuse)
- Privilege escalation attempts
- Unauthorized access attempts to admin endpoints

### 3. Security Metrics Dashboard
Create security analytics endpoint:
- `GET /admin-analytics/security-metrics`

Return metrics:
- Total authentication failures (24h, 7d, 30d)
- Failed login attempts by user
- Failed login attempts by IP address
- Suspicious IP addresses (blocked or flagged)
- Active security incidents
- Authentication success rate
- Token expiration patterns
- Admin access patterns
- Unauthorized endpoint access attempts

### 4. Security Alerts Integration
- Integrate with existing alert system (`/admin-analytics/alerts`)
- Create security-specific alerts:
  - High failed login rate (>10 failures/hour)
  - Suspicious IP detection
  - Account compromise indicators
  - Unauthorized admin access attempts
- Alert severity levels (info, warning, critical)
- Alert acknowledgment workflow

### 5. Frontend Security Dashboard
- Add "Security" section to admin analytics UI
- Display security metrics:
  - Authentication failure trends (chart)
  - Top failed login users/IPs (table)
  - Suspicious activity timeline
  - Active security incidents
  - Security health score
- Interactive filtering (date range, user, IP)
- Export security reports (CSV)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Security metrics endpoint `/admin-analytics/security-metrics` implemented
- [ ] Authentication failure tracking functional
- [ ] Suspicious activity detection working
- [ ] Security alerts integrated with alert system
- [ ] Frontend security dashboard section added
- [ ] Security metrics displayed with charts/tables
- [ ] Real-time security alerts visible
- [ ] CSV export for security reports
- [ ] Performance: <200ms for security metrics query
- [ ] Code coverage: 75%+ for security monitoring

## Technical Details

### Security Metrics Model
```python
class SecurityMetrics(BaseModel):
    """Security monitoring metrics"""
    auth_failures_24h: int
    auth_failures_7d: int
    auth_failures_30d: int
    failed_logins_by_user: List[Dict[str, Any]]
    failed_logins_by_ip: List[Dict[str, Any]]
    suspicious_ips: List[Dict[str, Any]]
    active_security_incidents: int
    auth_success_rate: float
    security_health_score: float
    unauthorized_access_attempts: int
```

### Suspicious Activity Detection
```python
def detect_suspicious_activity(db: Session, time_window: timedelta) -> List[Dict]:
    """Detect suspicious authentication patterns"""
    threshold_time = datetime.utcnow() - time_window
    
    # Multiple failures from same IP
    suspicious_ips = db.query(
        AuthLog.ip_address,
        func.count(AuthLog.id).label('failure_count')
    ).filter(
        AuthLog.timestamp >= threshold_time,
        AuthLog.success == False
    ).group_by(
        AuthLog.ip_address
    ).having(
        func.count(AuthLog.id) > 10  # Threshold: 10+ failures
    ).all()
    
    return [{
        'ip_address': ip,
        'failure_count': count,
        'risk_level': 'high' if count > 20 else 'medium'
    } for ip, count in suspicious_ips]
```

## Dependencies
- Authentication service logs/audit trail
- Auth service API access (or shared database)
- Existing alert system (`/admin-analytics/alerts`)
- Frontend admin analytics UI

## Estimated Effort
20-24 hours (2.5-3 days)

## Related
- File: `server/admin_analytics_api.py` (add security endpoint)
- SPEC: SPEC-030 Operational Intelligence (Security Monitoring)
- Related: Auth service, SPEC-009 (RBAC)

# US-263: PDF Report Generation for Admin Analytics

## Objective
Implement PDF report generation for SPEC-030 Admin Analytics Console to enable professional executive reports and automated monthly summaries.

## Technical Tasks

### 1. PDF Generation Library
- Add ReportLab dependency (v4.0.7+, same as SPEC-027 invoices)
- Create PDF generation utility module
- Design PDF template structure:
  - Header with company logo/branding
  - Executive summary section
  - Detailed metrics sections
  - Charts/graphs (convert Chart.js to static images or use ReportLab charts)
  - Footer with generation timestamp

### 2. Report Types
Implement the following report types:

#### Executive Summary Report
- Platform health overview
- Key metrics (users, teams, revenue, churn)
- Growth trends
- Financial summary (MRR, ARR, LTV)
- Top risks and opportunities

#### Monthly Analytics Report
- Complete monthly metrics breakdown
- User engagement trends
- Revenue cohort analysis
- Churn analysis details
- Feature adoption statistics
- Performance metrics

#### Custom Date Range Report
- User-selectable date range
- All metrics filtered by date range
- Comparative analysis (vs previous period)
- Trend indicators (up/down arrows)

### 3. PDF Generation Endpoint
- `GET /admin-analytics/export/pdf`
- Query parameters:
  - `report_type`: executive_summary | monthly | custom
  - `date_range`: 30d | 90d | custom
  - `start_date`: ISO date (for custom range)
  - `end_date`: ISO date (for custom range)
- Generate PDF in memory or temp file
- Return PDF as downloadable file response
- Set appropriate Content-Type headers

### 4. Chart/Graph Integration
- Convert dashboard charts to PDF format:
  - Option 1: Use ReportLab's built-in charting
  - Option 2: Convert Chart.js canvas to image (canvas-to-image)
  - Option 3: Generate static chart images server-side
- Include charts in appropriate report sections:
  - Revenue trends chart
  - User growth chart
  - Engagement distribution chart
  - Churn risk distribution chart

### 5. Frontend PDF Export UI
- Add "Export PDF" button to admin analytics dashboard
- Modal/dialog for report configuration:
  - Report type selection
  - Date range picker
  - Include charts checkbox
  - Email delivery option (future)
- Show download progress indicator
- Handle download errors gracefully

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] PDF generation endpoint `/admin-analytics/export/pdf` functional
- [ ] Executive summary report generates correctly
- [ ] Monthly analytics report includes all metrics
- [ ] Custom date range reports work
- [ ] Charts/graphs included in PDF
- [ ] PDF file size: <5MB for typical reports
- [ ] PDF generation time: <10 seconds
- [ ] Professional formatting with branding
- [ ] Frontend export UI implemented
- [ ] Error handling for generation failures
- [ ] PDF files readable in standard PDF viewers

## Technical Details

### PDF Generation Example
```python
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter, A4
from reportlab.lib import colors
from reportlab.lib.units import inch
from reportlab.platypus import SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, Table
from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet

def generate_executive_summary_pdf(metrics: dict) -> bytes:
    """Generate executive summary PDF report"""
    buffer = BytesIO()
    doc = SimpleDocTemplate(buffer, pagesize=letter)
    
    story = []
    styles = getSampleStyleSheet()
    
    # Title
    story.append(Paragraph("Executive Summary Report", styles['Title']))
    story.append(Spacer(1, 0.2*inch))
    
    # Executive Summary
    story.append(Paragraph("Platform Health", styles['Heading2']))
    story.append(Paragraph(
        f"Platform Health Score: {metrics['platform_health_score']}",
        styles['Normal']
    ))
    
    # Metrics Table
    data = [
        ['Metric', 'Value'],
        ['Total Users', f"{metrics['total_users']:,}"],
        ['Active Teams', f"{metrics['total_teams']:,}"],
        ['MRR', f"${metrics['total_revenue_30d']:,.2f}"],
        ['Churn Rate', f"{metrics['churn_rate']*100:.1f}%"]
    ]
    table = Table(data, colWidths=[3*inch, 2*inch])
    story.append(table)
    
    # Build PDF
    doc.build(story)
    buffer.seek(0)
    return buffer.read()
```

### Frontend PDF Export
```javascript
async function exportPDF(reportType, dateRange) {
  try {
    const response = await fetch(
      `/admin-analytics/export/pdf?report_type=${reportType}&date_range=${dateRange}`,
      { headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}` }}
    );
    
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error('PDF generation failed');
    
    const blob = await response.blob();
    const url = window.URL.createObjectURL(blob);
    const a = document.createElement('a');
    a.href = url;
    a.download = `admin-analytics-${reportType}-${Date.now()}.pdf`;
    a.click();
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('PDF export failed:', error);
    alert('Failed to generate PDF report');
  }
}
```

## Dependencies
- ReportLab v4.0.7+ (same version as SPEC-027 invoices)
- PDF generation utilities (reuse patterns from SPEC-027)
- Chart conversion tools (if using Chart.js)
- Frontend date picker component

## Estimated Effort
20-24 hours (2.5-3 days)

## Related
- File: `server/admin_analytics_api.py` (add PDF endpoint)
- SPEC: SPEC-030 Export Capabilities (PDF reports)
- Related: SPEC-027 (invoice PDF generation patterns)

# US-264: Advanced Admin Tools for Admin Analytics Console

```python
async def enable_maintenance(
    message: str = Query("System maintenance in progress"),
    current_user: User = Depends(require_admin)
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Enable maintenance mode"""
    # Store maintenance mode in Redis/database
    # Notify active users
    # Allow admin access

        "enabled": True,
        "message": message,
        "enabled_by": current_user.email,

```

### User Impersonation
```python
@router.post("/support/impersonate/{user_id}")
async def impersonate_user(
    user_id: int,
    current_user: User = Depends(require_admin),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db)
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Start impersonating a user (admin only)"""
    # Security check
    if not current_user.is_admin:
        raise HTTPException(403, "Admin access required")
    
    # Get target user
    target_user = db.query(User).filter(User.id == user_id).first()
    if not target_user:
        raise HTTPException(404, "User not found")
    
    # Create impersonation session
    impersonation_token = create_impersonation_token(
        admin_user_id=current_user.id,
        target_user_id=user_id
    )
    
    # Audit log
    log_admin_action(
        admin_id=current_user.id,
        action="impersonate_user",
        target_user_id=user_id
    )
    
    return {
        "impersonation_token": impersonation_token,
        "target_user": target_user.email,
        "expires_at": (datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(hours=1)).isoformat()
    }
```

- Frontend admin console UI

- Related: SPEC-005 (Admin Dashboard), RBAC system

subject: US-265: Redis Caching Integration for Admin Analytics
description:
# US-265: Redis Caching Integration for Admin Analytics

## Objective
Replace in-memory caching in SPEC-030 Admin Analytics API with Redis for distributed caching, improved performance, and cache sharing across service instances.

## Technical Tasks

### 1. Redis Integration Setup
- Add Redis client dependency (redis-py)
- Configure Redis connection:
  - Connection pool configuration
  - Error handling and reconnection logic
  - Health check for Redis availability
  - Environment variable configuration (REDIS_URL)

### 2. Cache Strategy Implementation
Replace in-memory cache with Redis:

#### Cache Keys
- `admin_analytics:platform_metrics` - Platform overview (TTL: 15 min)
- `admin_analytics:churn_analysis` - Churn data (TTL: 30 min)
- `admin_analytics:revenue_cohorts` - Revenue data (TTL: 60 min)
- `admin_analytics:user_engagement` - Engagement metrics (TTL: 15 min)
- `admin_analytics:business_intelligence` - BI dashboard (TTL: 15 min)

#### Cache Patterns
- Cache-aside pattern (check cache, if miss query DB, store in cache)
- Cache invalidation on data updates
- TTL-based expiration
- Namespace prefixes to avoid key collisions

### 3. Cache Utility Functions
Create reusable cache utilities:
- `get_cached(key, default=None)` - Get from cache
- `set_cached(key, value, ttl=900)` - Set in cache with TTL
- `invalidate_cache(pattern)` - Invalidate matching keys
- `clear_analytics_cache()` - Clear all analytics cache

### 4. Update Existing Endpoints
Replace in-memory cache with Redis in:
- `GET /admin-analytics/platform-overview`
- `GET /admin-analytics/churn-analysis`
- `GET /admin-analytics/revenue-cohorts`
- `GET /admin-analytics/user-engagement`
- `GET /admin-analytics/business-intelligence`

### 5. Cache Invalidation Strategy
Implement cache invalidation triggers:
- On user/team data updates
- On subscription/billing changes
- Manual cache clear endpoint (admin only)
- Scheduled cache refresh (optional, background job)

### 6. Performance Monitoring
- Track cache hit/miss rates
- Monitor Redis connection health
- Log cache performance metrics
- Add cache stats to admin analytics dashboard

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Redis integration functional
- [ ] All endpoints use Redis caching
- [ ] Cache hit/miss rates tracked
- [ ] Cache invalidation working correctly
- [ ] Graceful degradation if Redis unavailable (fallback to no cache)
- [ ] Performance: <100ms cache retrieval
- [ ] Cache shared across service instances
- [ ] Cache TTLs configured appropriately
- [ ] Redis health monitoring in place
- [ ] Code coverage: 80%+ for cache layer

## Technical Details

### Redis Cache Implementation
```python
import redis
from typing import Any, Optional
import json
from datetime import timedelta

class AnalyticsCache:
    """Redis-based cache for admin analytics"""
    
    def __init__(self, redis_url: str):
        self.redis_client = redis.from_url(redis_url, decode_responses=True)
        self.namespace = "admin_analytics"
    
    def _make_key(self, key: str) -> str:
        return f"{self.namespace}:{key}"
    
    def get(self, key: str) -> Optional[Any]:
        """Get value from cache"""
        try:
            cached = self.redis_client.get(self._make_key(key))
            if cached:
                return json.loads(cached)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning(f"Cache get failed: {e}")
        return None
    
    def set(self, key: str, value: Any, ttl: int = 900) -> bool:
        """Set value in cache with TTL"""
        try:
            serialized = json.dumps(value, default=str)
            return self.redis_client.setex(
                self._make_key(key),
                ttl,
                serialized
            )
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning(f"Cache set failed: {e}")
            return False
    
    def invalidate(self, pattern: str) -> int:
        """Invalidate matching cache keys"""
        try:
            keys = self.redis_client.keys(self._make_key(pattern))
            if keys:
                return self.redis_client.delete(*keys)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning(f"Cache invalidation failed: {e}")
        return 0
```

### Updated Endpoint Example
```python
@router.get("/platform-overview")
async def get_platform_overview(
    current_user: User = Depends(require_admin),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db)
) -> PlatformMetrics:
    """Get high-level platform metrics with Redis caching"""
    
    # Check cache
    cache_key = "platform_metrics"
    cached = analytics_cache.get(cache_key)
    if cached:
        return PlatformMetrics(**cached)
    
    # Query database
    metrics = calculate_platform_metrics(db)
    
    # Cache result (15 minutes)
    analytics_cache.set(cache_key, metrics.dict(), ttl=900)
    
    return metrics
```

### Cache Invalidation
```python
@router.post("/cache/invalidate")
async def invalidate_cache(
    pattern: str = Query("*"),
    current_user: User = Depends(require_admin)
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Invalidate analytics cache (admin only)"""
    invalidated_count = analytics_cache.invalidate(pattern)
    return {
        "success": True,
        "pattern": pattern,
        "invalidated_keys": invalidated_count
    }
```

- redis-py library
- Redis connection configuration
- Environment variables (REDIS_URL)

# US-266: Support Metrics Analysis for Admin Analytics

## Objective
Implement support metrics analysis in SPEC-030 Admin Analytics Console to track common issues, feature requests, and user feedback patterns for data-driven product improvements.

## Technical Tasks

### 1. Support Data Integration
Identify and integrate support data sources:
- Support ticket system (if exists)
- User feedback submissions
- Feature request system
- Error logs and stack traces
- User-reported issues
- In-app feedback widgets

### 2. Support Metrics Endpoint
Create `/admin-analytics/support-metrics` endpoint:

Return metrics:
- **Common Issues**: Top 10 most reported issues
  - Issue category (bug, feature request, question, billing)
  - Issue count and frequency
  - Average resolution time
  - Affected user count

- **Feature Requests**: Most requested features
  - Feature name/description
  - Request count
  - User votes/priority
  - Status (pending, in-progress, completed)

- **Support Volume**: Support ticket trends
  - Tickets per day/week/month
  - Ticket volume trends (growing/declining)
  - Average response time
  - Average resolution time
  - Ticket backlog size

- **Issue Categories**: Breakdown by category
  - Bug reports
  - Feature requests
  - Billing issues
  - Technical support
  - Account issues
  - Other

- **User Satisfaction**: Support quality metrics
  - Support ticket satisfaction ratings
  - Average resolution time by category
  - First-contact resolution rate
  - Escalation rate

### 3. Issue Pattern Detection
Implement pattern detection algorithms:
- Identify recurring issues (same issue from multiple users)
- Detect issue trends (increasing/decreasing frequency)
- Correlate issues with product releases
- Identify user segments with higher support needs
- Detect support quality issues (long resolution times)

### 4. Frontend Support Dashboard
- Add "Support Analytics" section to admin analytics UI
- Display:
  - Common issues table (sortable, filterable)
  - Feature requests list with priority/votes
  - Support volume trends chart
  - Issue category breakdown (pie/bar chart)
  - Resolution time metrics
- Interactive features:
  - Filter by date range
  - Filter by issue category

### 5. Support Alert Integration

  - High support volume spikes
  - Critical issues affecting multiple users
  - Long average resolution times
  - Feature requests reaching threshold (e.g., 50+ requests)

## Acceptance Criteria

## Technical Details

### Common Issues Detection
```python
def detect_common_issues(db: Session, days: int = 30) -> List[Dict]:
    """Identify most common support issues"""
    cutoff_date = datetime.utcnow() - timedelta(days=days)
    
    # Query support tickets/issues
    issues = db.query(
        SupportTicket.category,
        SupportTicket.title,
        func.count(SupportTicket.id).label('count'),
        func.avg(SupportTicket.resolution_time_hours).label('avg_resolution')
    ).filter(
        SupportTicket.created_at >= cutoff_date
    ).group_by(
        SupportTicket.category,
        SupportTicket.title
    ).order_by(
        func.count(SupportTicket.id).desc()
    ).limit(10).all()
    
    return [{
        'category': cat,
        'title': title,
        'count': count,
        'avg_resolution_hours': float(avg_resolution) if avg_resolution else None
    } for cat, title, count, avg_resolution in issues]
```

### Feature Requests Analysis
```python
def analyze_feature_requests(db: Session) -> List[Dict]:
    """Analyze feature request patterns"""
    requests = db.query(
        FeatureRequest.title,
        FeatureRequest.description,
        func.count(FeatureRequest.id).label('request_count'),
        func.sum(FeatureRequest.votes).label('total_votes'),
        FeatureRequest.status
    ).group_by(
        FeatureRequest.title,
        FeatureRequest.description,
        FeatureRequest.status
    ).order_by(
        func.sum(FeatureRequest.votes).desc()
    ).all()
    
    return [{
        'title': title,
        'description': desc,
        'request_count': count,
        'total_votes': votes or 0,
        'status': status
    } for title, desc, count, votes, status in requests]
```
